_provenance.notes: Cook Inlet beluga whales (Delphinapterus leucas) are a distinct, isolated population of about 279 animals (2022 estimate) found only in Cook Inlet, Alaska. They were hunted to near-extinction by Alaska Native subsistence hunters between 1994-1998, when the population fell from ~1,000 to ~350 animals in just 4 years. The population was listed as Endangered under ESA in 2008. Recovery is considered unlikely before 2100 under current conditions due to small population size, lack of recruitment, habitat degradation, and vessel noise impacts. Their primary prey is Chinook and sockeye salmon, directly linking their recovery to salmon abundance in Cook Inlet.

fisheries_connection.salmon_dependency: Belugas follow salmon up the Kenai, Little Susitna, and Susitna Rivers. Decline in Chinook salmon in Cook Inlet has been identified as a contributing factor to beluga non-recovery.
threats: Ship strike (vessel traffic in Anchorage area)
Contamination (PCBs, heavy metals from Anchorage urban runoff)
Unusual Mortality Events (UME) — strandings in tidal flats
Climate change effects on prey distribution
